result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A puts 24px between cards, which is larger than every gap inside a card (the largest is 16px). That directly meets the requirement that card spacing exceed internal spacing, and its spacing comes from a small 4px-based scale. B's 16px card gap is smaller than its own 20px synopsis-to-buttons gap and its 20px padding, so it fails item 3. B separates the buttons more clearly (20px vs 12px, where A uses 16px vs 12px) but uses more distinct spacing values. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers group the title with the author at 4px and separate the buttons from the text. Answer B's 24px card gap is larger than every gap inside a card, while Answer A's 16px card gap is smaller than its 20px gap above the buttons, so A misses rubric item 3. B also builds its spacing from a small set of repeated 4px-based tokens, while A uses more one-off values (4, 8, 12, 16, 20).
